From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@healthloop.com>, Devon Park <devon.park@healthloop.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP prep: quick econ checkpoints for HealthLoop meeting

Clara / Devon —

Thanks for the sample traffic. I imported the CSV and updated the workbook with a worked example; attaching the exports: token-econ-breakdown.csv and a short notes PDF (redwood-econ-notes.pdf). Highlights:

- Billable tokens model: we bill at the token granularity after cache application. Prefix cache: if the prefix is a hit we charge only for the continuation (delta tokens). Full KV cache (exact completion hit) results in 0 billable tokens for that request. I flagged the workbook cells where we applied 40% prefix-hit and 5% exact-hit for conservative scenario.

- Batching effects: with continuous batching on our runtime, latency-sensitive chat keeps smaller micro-batches (avg batch size 3 at 90th percentile) — we modeled that as a 12% unit-cost premium vs max-efficiency batching. For summarization (background), we modeled large batches (avg 16) that lower unit cost by ~48%. See "scenario_summary" tab.

- Tail latency: to hold 95th <350ms at 8k context for triage chat we routable to reserved dedicated nodes with a slightly higher per-token price; I included a break-even calc (column G) showing when dedicated vs hosted becomes cheaper given concurrency.

Open items that should sit in the MAP as acceptance gates:
  • Pilot traffic profile to be timestamped & uploaded to Drive within 5 business days (HealthLoop)
  • Acceptance thresholds: cost variance <15% vs modeled MAP scenarios after 2-week smoke test
  • Caching instrumentation: HealthLoop to include trace id on requests so we can validate prefix/exact hit rates

Callouts for procurement: we'll provide a printable one-pager that defines what counts as billable tokens post-cache and a short clause for pilot credits if measured costs exceed the conservative scenario by >20% during the pilot.

Next: Thursday call — I can walk the workbook and then we can convert the highlighted acceptance gates into the MAP milestones.

Cheers,
Mateo
Redwood Inference

Attachments: token-econ-breakdown.csv, redwood-econ-notes.pdf

From: Devon Park <devon.park@healthloop.com>

Thanks — couple clarifying items after skimming the notes:

1) The 40% prefix-hit assumption: is that for chat prompts where we have a lot of shared templates, or an aggregate number across both chat & summarization? We expect chat to have higher reuse but summarization almost none.
2) For the "trace id" instrumentation ask: our engineering team prefers not to send PII in headers. Can the instrumentation be implemented with a non-PII correlation id?

Also — on the dedicated vs hosted cost calc: can you show a sample run-rate (12-month) that includes expected growth (10% month-over-month) so procurement can see longer-term impact?

We want the MAP to be explicit about when we flip from hosted to dedicated capacity during expansion.

—Devon
Senior Eng Manager, Platform
HealthLoop

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@healthloop.com>, Devon Park <devon.park@healthloop@healthloop.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, procure@healthloop.com

Subject: Re: MAP economics: tokens/$, caching & batching assumptions — next steps and MAP gates

Clara / Devon —

Great questions. Short answers + MAP updates we will include before the call: 

1) Prefix-hit assumption: adjusted. In the updated workbook (final slide + appendix) we split hit-rate by workload: chat = 55% prefix-hit, summarization = 8% prefix-hit. Those are conservative estimates based on similar telehealth pilots and your sample.

2) Instrumentation: agreed — use a non-PII correlation id. We'll add an instrumentation spec to the MAP that lists required keys (correlation_id, request_type, model_variant) and sample headers.

3) 12-month run-rate: we added a growth tab with 10% MoM compounding and a transition model that flags break-even month to switch to Dedicated (by default at 70% of sustained concurrency and 60% of committed tokens). That run-rate page is one-click export to PDF for procurement.

MAP acceptance gates (to appear in the doc):
  • Upload: HealthLoop traffic sample to Drive (by 2028-07-24)
  • Smoke test: 14-day pilot with cost/latency telemetry enabled; cost delta must be <=15% vs MAP expected scenario or Redwood will allocate a pilot credit (TBD)
  • Dedicated trigger: sustained 3-week average exceedance of committed tokens/concurrency thresholds (auto-eval in console)

Mateo will present the workbook on Thursday 10:00 PT. After the call we'll convert the highlighted cells into the shared MAP spreadsheet and produce the one-pager for Procurement.

Thanks — see you Thursday.
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
